claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! I need to start by understanding your situation. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about the children involved.

**First question: How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

The eligibility rules differ depending on the child's age:
- **Under 16 years old** - generally eligible if other conditions are met
- **16-19 years old** - eligible if they're in full-time education or training
- **20 years or older** - not eligible for Child Benefit

Please tell me the age(s) of the child/children you're inquiring about, and I'll guide you through the rest of the process.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible. I have a young one - Alex is 3 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information! Alex is 3 years old, which means Alex is under 16. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check the next criterion. 

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is only 3 years old, I expect the answer is yes, but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 3! They're just at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for a 3-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I'm asking whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit in their own right

For a 3-year-old, the answer is almost certainly yes (they're not receiving these), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name - they're just a toddler!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

This is checking whether Alex is in a disqualifying apprenticeship (regional rules apply). Given that Alex is only 3 years old, the answer should be no, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - Alex is only 3, so no apprenticeship or anything like that!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! Since Alex is not in an apprenticeship, let me continue to the next important check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important criterion: **your residency status in the UK**.

There are several ways you could qualify based on residency. Let me ask you about your situation:

**Do any of the following apply to you?**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - this is the main route
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** - if you're from the EU/EEA
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively looking for work (can claim for up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources and aren't claiming certain benefits, OR
   - You're a student with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these (if any) describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live here in the UK - I'm in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check: **Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility means at least one of the following:

1. **You live with Alex** - you're their main carer in the household
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - you pay for things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, or other care (can be weekly, monthly, or lump sum payments) at least equivalent to Child Benefit
3. **You're paying maintenance** - under a court order or agreement, where payments cover Alex's upkeep and equal or exceed Child Benefit

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me - I'm their main carer.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live with Alex and are their main carer, so you're responsible for them. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check: **Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child. 

**Does anyone else claim Child Benefit for Alex?** For example:
- The other parent
- A grandparent
- Another family member

Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're the only one claiming for Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Where is Alex currently living?**

Specifically:
- **Is Alex in hospital?**
- **Is Alex in care** (residential care, secure accommodation, etc.)?
- **Is Alex being fostered?**
- **Or is Alex living at home with you normally?**

Which one applies to Alex's situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living at home with me normally - nothing special like hospital or care or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! We're nearly there. **Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Are you paying for Alex's accommodation (housing) and maintenance yourself?
- Or is the local council paying for any part of Alex's accommodation or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm paying for everything myself for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's the final check complete. Let me now provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! 🎉

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit! ✓**

### Summary
You meet all the eligibility requirements for claiming Child Benefit for **Alex**. Here's why you qualify:

✓ Alex is 3 years old (under 16 years old)
✓ Alex is not working full-time
✓ Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in their own right
✓ Alex is not in any disqualifying apprenticeship
✓ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
✓ You live with Alex and are their main carer
✓ No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✓ Alex is living at home with you normally
✓ You are paying for all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance yourself

### Next Steps - How to Claim

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some of this back through self-assessment
5. **Payment frequency** - you'll receive payments every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### Useful Links
- [How to claim Child Benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim)
- [High Income Child Benefit Charge](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/high-income-child-benefit-charge)

Congratulations on your eligibility! If you have any other questions or need help with anything else, feel free to ask.
